quote: Statute text read on azleg.gov (43-1011(D)): "the department shall adjust the income dollar amount for each rate bracket" (Phoenix CPI) -- but that applies to the graduated schedule. The only figure covered is a single band starting at 0 (flat 2.5% since 2023, per the ADOR 2025 Form 140 booklet), so there is no threshold to adjust.
notes: The azleg.gov page fetched still showed the pre-flat-rate graduated table (2.59% to 4.5%) with subsection D indexing; I could not read the text that sets the flat 2.5% rate. With one band at 0 nothing grows either way. If a graduated schedule ever returns, 43-1011(D) indexes the bracket amounts to the metropolitan Phoenix CPI.

quote: Georgia taxes at a single flat rate (5.19% for 2025): 'the tax imposed pursuant to subsection (a) of this Code section shall be 5.19 percent ... for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025' (as shown, before amendment, in HB 463 (2026)).
notes: One band starting at 0, so no threshold exists to index. The rate itself steps down on a schedule (0.10 point a year, conditional on revenue tests), which is a rate schedule, not an inflation index. The official O.C.G.A. text itself is on a Lexis site not readable here; the wording was read in the bill text on legis.ga.gov that quotes the existing code.

quote: (B) A standard deduction in an amount as follows: (i) In the case of a married couple filing a joint return, $24,000.00 ...; (ii) In the case of a single taxpayer, head of household, or married taxpayer filing a separate return, $12,000.00 ...
notes: Fixed amounts in current law. HB 463 of 2026 ('As passed House and Senate'; signature status not checked) would raise them to $30,000/$15,000 for 2026 and then by $750/$375 a year to $36,000/$18,000, delayed in years the revenue tests fail. That would be a fixed schedule, not inflation indexing, and does not affect tax year 2025.

quote: The tax commissioner shall prescribe new rate schedules that apply in lieu of the schedules set forth in subdivisions a through e. For this purpose, the rate applicable to each income bracket may not be changed
notes: The code PDF read is an older edition (its listed brackets differ from the 2025 figures), but subdivision g is the standing rule.
